question:
A 17-year-old male is brought to the emergency department after a motor vehicle collision. He has
multiple injuries and is minimally responsive. Notable findings include a large laceration on his
forehead, a nasal bridge fracture, and coughing with blood in his oropharynx. He is wearing a soft
cervical collar. Vital signs are: temperature 36.4°C, blood pressure 115/75 mmHg, heart rate 126 bpm,
respiratory rate 17 breaths per minute, and oxygen saturation 88% on room air. He has received 2
liters of intravenous normal saline via 2 peripheral IV lines during transport. Examination reveals frank
blood in the oropharynx, bilateral breath sounds, a distended and tender abdomen, and weak (1+)
pulses. What should be the initial step in managing this patient? Answer Choices: (A) Focused
Assessment with Sonography for Trauma (FAST) scan (B) Cricothyroidotomy (C) Rapid sequence
intubation (D) Bag-valve mask ventilation (E) Emergency thoracotomy (F) Needle decompression (G)
Orotracheal intubation (H) Emergency tracheostomy (I) Direct laryngoscopy (J) Nasotracheal
intubation
 A. Focused Assessment with Sonography for Trauma (FAST) scan
B. Orotracheal intubation
C. Emergency tracheostomy
D. Rapid sequence intubation
E. Needle decompression
F. Bag-valve mask ventilation
G. Emergency thoracotomy
H. Direct laryngoscopy
I. Cricothyroidotomy
J. Nasotracheal intubation
